Welcome to chilton trinity school
Work Hard. Be Kind. Be Ambitious. Be Curious. Be Proud.
Welcome
As Headteacher of Chilton Trinity School, I am extremely proud to welcome you on behalf of everyone in our thriving and purposeful 11–16 school community, serving Bridgwater and the surrounding areas.
Working with students, families, staff and other members of our wider community, we have reshaped our shared Mission, Vision and Values to ensure they truly reflect who we are as a school:
Our Mission:
A school community where everyone belongs, everyone is valued, and everyone can thrive
Our Vision:
Success Breeds Success
Our Values:
Work Hard – Be Kind – Be Ambitious – Be Curious – Be Proud
This collaborative project marked a pivotal stage in our school improvement journey. Our Mission, Vision and Values now guide every decision we make for every member of our school community, enabling everyone to thrive and fulfil their potential.
We were delighted when Ofsted inspected the school in September 2024 and judged Chilton Trinity to be ‘Good’ in every area of the Ofsted Framework:
The Quality of Education
Behaviour and Attitudes
Personal Development
Leadership and Management
We are very proud of this outcome, which is a testament to the dedication and commitment of our staff, who work tirelessly to support every student.
Our aim at Chilton Trinity is simple. Within a safe and supportive environment, we strive to provide a high-quality educational experience in which students are known, valued and cared for by our exceptional pastoral team, while being academically challenged to become the very best they can be.
We work hard to remove barriers to learning so that every student has the opportunity to achieve academic success and make informed choices about their next steps beyond school.
We make no apology for having high expectations of every member of our school community in relation to attendance, behaviour and academic achievement. Our students understand that it is not enough simply to attend school every day. They are expected to embrace every opportunity available to them, both within the classroom and through our strong House system, extracurricular activities, trips and visits.
We have worked hard to create a strong school community where everyone experiences a genuine sense of belonging, built on mutual trust and respect. We are relentless in expecting the very best from everyone, maintaining high standards and continually improving in areas where we know we can do better. Only the best is good enough for our students, and we expect the best from them in return.
As trusted educational professionals, we are grateful for the support of our parents and carers. Every decision we make is guided by the best interests of our students and our determination to strengthen their potential for both academic and personal success.
We are proud to be part of the Futura Learning Partnership, a family of 26 primary and secondary schools across the South West. Being part of the Trust provides valuable opportunities to collaborate with excellent practitioners and share expertise that can positively influence every aspect of school life.
The shared Futura Learning Partnership values of Respect, Opportunity, Collaboration and Aspiration underpin everything we do. We greatly value Futura’s support and its encouragement for each school to retain and celebrate the distinctive identity of the local community it serves.
There is so much more to discover about Chilton Trinity School, and we are always delighted to welcome visitors. If you would like to arrange a visit, please contact our Reception Manager, Miss H McElligott, in the first instance on 01278 425222.
Ms K DeadyHeadteacher, Chilton Trinity School

all saints as a church school
At All Saints Church of England Primary School, we are proud of our Christian Foundation which is rooted in our involvement with our local Church - All Saints.
All Saints as a Church School
We value our church foundation and how this makes our school a special place to be.
At All Saints Church of England Primary School, we are proud of our Christian Foundation which is rooted in our involvement with our local Church- All Saints.
Our Siams Inspection Sept 2024) assessed that ‘the school creates a culture of exceptional care and encouragement. This is inspired by the vision of a ‘nurturing environment’, reflecting Christian care for its community. This ensures that adults and pupils are treated well.’
The school was built for the community of East Clevedon and we welcome all pupils and their families of all faiths or none to live out our Vision Statement ‘Inspired to learn’ and to carry out Proverbs 22:6 where, as a community “we start children off on the way they should go and even when they are old they will not turn from it.
Church Links
All Saints Church was founded in 1860 and celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2010.
In 1870 the Church, together with the Diocese of Bath and Wells, built All Saints School.
In those days it started as a Sunday School, but quickly developed into an Infants and Primary school serving this community. The school has been supported by the church ever since.
Across the Diocese, we have some 33,000 children currently in church schools. The added value that the ethos and heritage of church schools contributes has been strongly recognised by different Governments over the years and many parents rightly see them as healthy and good schools.
Our aim here, as we seek to support the school, is to be a friend and resource. Our Church building is used on a daily basis by the school, we have weekly Collective Worship taken by the clergy of the church, whole school services for festivals, we provide 3 Foundation Governors to assist in leading the school and we provide pastoral support when needed. We are pleased that our relationship with the school is warm, strong and supportive.
The Diocese takes as its guiding principal some words of Christ found in John’s Gospel – “I have come that they might have life, and have it to the full”. This is what a healthy and positive partnership between the School and Church feels like and at All Saints Church, we hope that our partnership with All Saints East Clevedon Church of England Primary School contributes to this fulfilment and enjoyment of learning and living.
Fr Noel HectorRector of All Saints Church and Rural Dean of Portishead
www.eastclevedonchurches.co.ukeastcleveub@blueyonder.co.uk(01275) 872357
Collective Worship
Through our collective worship provision we aim to encourage children’s natural sense of wonder and to develop their qualities of curiosity, celebration, faith and gratitude which form the foundation of the worship of God.
Through this we want to contribute to children’s spiritual, moral and cultural development and enable them to reflect specifically on Christian values and beliefs.
To engage our children and provide a variety of approaches to collective worship, we aim to foster a sense of community and unity within the school.
We aspire to offer children an opportunity for the understanding of God in a way that is individual and appropriate for them, and which allows them to be comfortable in worship.
During our Siams Inspection (sept 2024) it was referenced that: ‘Collective worship is central to the school day and has a significant impact on enabling all to flourish spiritually.’
Collective Worship Policy
Each week we congregate to celebrate our collective worship in All Saints Church led by Father Noel. The positioning of our school enables this regular link and our children respect the church as a place of worship.
Our Collective Worship builds on our school values of; Community, Creativity, Joy, Curiosity and Confidence. Each term we explore a Value in depth. the photo below shows our display of Joy from our school Collective Worship responses and our own celebration of our pilgrimage to Wells Cathedral to see the Gaia Exhibit.

We aim to have a range of approaches which ensure pupils remain engaged and excited by our Collective Worship.

All Saints Church of England Primary School was first build as a Sunday school, but the Elton family and gifted to the local Church. From 1873 the school opened as a day school for the children of the local community.

We are a primary academy within the Futura Learning Partnership.
Our school is set in the beautiful Swiss style valley, with close links with All Saints Church, with whom we share a number of spaces, including the Church hall and Glebe field.
Our School
We are a primary academy within the Futura Learning Partnership.
Welcome to All Saints Church of England Primary School.
We are incredibly proud to welcome you to All Saints, a thriving and nurturing primary school at the heart of our community — and now the home of our highly successful preschool. Opening the preschool has been a wonderful milestone for us, giving our youngest learners the very best start to their education in a warm, supportive and inspiring environment.
Within our school, children develop a strong sense of belonging and a vibrant learning community. Positive relationships are at the centre of everything we do. Every child is valued, nurtured and encouraged, while also being challenged academically so they can flourish and achieve their full potential.
Ofsted (2023) recognised our strengths, stating:
“This warm and welcoming school is highly valued by the community it serves. Leaders’ vision to promote pupils’ ‘curiosity and confidence’ threads through all that the school does.”
Creativity and a love of learning lie at the heart of our curriculum. Our pupils immerse themselves enthusiastically in their work, supported by a dedicated and highly experienced staff team; many of whom have been part of All Saints for many years. We are deeply proud of our children’s achievements, our staff’s professionalism, and the strong partnerships we share with families and the wider community.
Our SIAMS inspection (Sept 2024) also highlighted the strength of our ethos:
“All Saints is an exceptionally warm and nurturing community where adults and pupils are treated well… Strong, supportive, collaborative relationships are central to school life.”
All Saints has a rich history. Our Victorian building first opened as a primary school on 28th June 1873, and we were delighted to celebrate 150 years of education in 2023. Between 2016 and 2018 the school underwent significant redevelopment, including a new four‑classroom block, modernised facilities and the addition of Saxby Cottage. Today, our children enjoy spacious classrooms, up‑to‑date technology and a learning environment designed for both comfort and inspiration.
We make full use of every part of our site and are fortunate to rent the Church Hall and the Glebe Field, which provide additional space for play, PE and outdoor learning.
At All Saints, we have high expectations for every child — personally, socially and academically. As a small school, we know our pupils well and help them become confident, capable learners ready for the next stage of their education. Children regularly take part in whole‑school performances and presentations from Reception onwards, helping them grow in confidence and creativity.
School Day:The lower gates open at 8:45am, giving children time to settle with classroom activities before the school day begins at 8:50am. The day ends at 3:20pm.

If you have any questions about our school, please do contact us — I would be delighted to talk with you.

Team Vision
We want our students to be excited about the world and to have an appreciation and understanding of different cultures. We want our students to be effective communicators, empathetic citizens, intellectually curious and economically mobile. We want to provoke thought and curiosity through activities that reflect their interests in the modern world. Ultimately, we want our students to see and experience a world without barriers and become global citizens.

SEND and Inclusion
You can find all the information you need about our SEND policies.
The school’s SENDCo is Mrs Rachel Mills
We are a fully inclusive school and meet the diverse needs of every child in the school. Our Siams Inspection (Sept 2024) summarised the support of individuals : ‘As a result of far-sighted actions by the leaders and staff, the potential of pupils identified as disadvantaged is being transformed.’
Staff work closely with parents to ensure that children’s needs are quickly and effectively identified and that appropriate support is provided or sought.
We acknowledge that some children will develop special educational needs at some time in their school career. Sometimes these can be met by short term targeted support or adapting learning tasks. For some children, their needs will be met by a range of in class, and additional adult support, at times other educational specialists may be involved.
Children may also require an Individual Education Plan (IEP) drawn up by the class teacher, with the support of the special needs co-coordinator (SENCO), and in consultation with the parents. A close partnership with parents is essential to identify a child’s needs and how to meet those needs. A copy of the Special Educational Needs policy can be found within the documents section below.
The children benefit from additional in-class support from a Teaching Assistant or Learning Support Assistant and sometimes work in small groups out of the classroom environment.
We follow a graduated approach – Assess – Plan – Do and Review
The four main SEND areas are (as identified by the SEND Code of Practice):
1. Communication and Interaction.
2. Cognition and Learning.
3. Social, Emotional and Mental Health difficulties.
4. Physical and/or Sensory Needs.
We identify and focus on these categories for our children who may need additional support.
Our School SENDco is Mrs. Rachel Mills.
Should you wish to contact Mrs. Mills, please phone the school- 01275 874169 or email; office@allsaintsprimaryschool.org.uk

Art Curriculum Overview
“A work of art which did not begin in emotion is not art.” – Paul Cézanne
“Creativity takes courage.” – Henri Matisse
“Art washes away from the soul the dust of everyday life.” – Pablo Picasso
Art Curriculum Team Vision
Promote creativity, imagination and self-expression.
Rich and diverse cultural experience.

Art Curriculum Intent
Key Stage 3
Students produce original, imaginative and personal work.
Key Stage 4
When and why.
Year 7 focuses on basic skill building to ensure a strong foundation from which to explore the subject. Key skills such as drawing and painting are re visited and built upon in Year 8 and 9 – Art is a skill-based subject and skills take practice. Throughout KS3 students produce projects in a similar style to GCSE so that those who opt for the subject in Year 10 have a good understanding of how to approach their coursework. In KS4 pupils produce highly personalised work and spend Year 10 producing projects towards their Component 1 portfolio. These projects start more guided and gradually allow a wider choice of artists and approaches as scaffolding is removed. The last project in Year 10 is set up as a mock of the externally set task so that students have a chance to experience the controlled practical element they will do in Component 2 of Year 11. At the start of Year 11 students revisit their projects from Year 10, improving and selecting work for their portfolios before undertaking the Component 2 externally set task in January.

English Curriculum Overview
Team Vision
The English department at Chilton Trinity School inspires a love of literature, language and learning through our curriculum and teaching. Our curriculum has been designed to be inclusive of all our students, giving them the ability to see themselves reflected within the books and texts we study. Our curriculum challenges students to think independently, develop curiosity and become autonomous individuals.
Curriculum Intent
As the starting point of a student’s secondary English learning journey, it is vital that English at Key Stage 3 not only enables students to flourish in their creativity, communication and textual exploration, but that it builds on the firm foundations established at KS2 and successfully underpins what students will go on to study at KS4.
The English curriculum provides students with opportunities to explore a range of fiction and non-fiction texts: developing, mastering and extending analytical skills, creativity in written work and clear communication. Topics and texts span a range of eras, cultures and viewpoints and support students’ consideration and evaluation of how context, reader knowledge and attitude as well as writer’s craft can affect how a text is both produced and received. Equally, through addressing such vital themes as relationships, bias and individuality, immigration, morality and politics, students are frequently provided with opportunities to develop their empathy and wider understanding of the world. This exploration promotes and encourages enquiry, as well as developing and mastering an understanding of linguistic conventions and vocabulary, which in turn supports students in their verbal and written communication. human beings.
